 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To
Mandamus Directing The Respondents To Pass An
Award Determining Compensation For Which The
Petitioner Is Entitle To Receive In Respect Of The
Lands Which Was Acquired For Construction Of Road
And To Pay Them Compensation They Are Entitled To
Receive Also Direct The Respondents To Pay The
Amount Of Compensation Under 4 (1) Notification To
The Extent Land Acquired By Them "Annexure-B" Dated
10/11/1999 Vide Sum/Kum/Bhuswa/37/98-99.
 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

In this writ petition, the petitioner is seeking direction to the respondents to pass an award,
determining the compensation to the extent of land acquired by respondent-authorities in terms of notification dated 10.11.1999, produced at Annexure-B to the writ petition.
2. It is the grievance of the petitioner that, the petitioner is the owner in possession of the land situate at NC: 2023:KHC-K:6253 Wachha village, Chittapur Taluk, Kalaburagi District.
It is stated in the writ petition that, the respondents have acquired the schedule land for public purpose to lay road from Madabul to Kodli, however, no compensation is granted to the petitioner.
Hence, this writ petition is filed.

3. I have heard Smt. Sharada Patil, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Smt.Maya T.R.,
learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent-State.

4. Smt. Sharada Patil, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that, though the land belonging to the petitioner has been acquired during the year, 1999 by issuing preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act, and roads have been laid, however,
compensation has not been granted to the petitioner and therefore, she submits that, it is clear violation of Article 300-A of Constitution of India.
Accordingly, she sought for interference of this Court.

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, Smt. Maya T.R., learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent-State disputes the acquisition of the land belonging to the petitioner.
She further submitted that, though the preliminary notification has been issued on 10.11.1999, however, no action has been taken to issue final notification nor award is passed.
Hence, she submitted that, the writ petition deserves to be dismissed in limine.
6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, the relief sought for by the petitioner is with regard to issuance of writ of mandamus to acquire the land belonging to the petitioner.
It is well established principle in law that, it is eminent domain on the part of the respondent-authorities to acquire land, if it is required for public purpose.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramanik Lal N Bhutta vs. State of Maharastra reported in AIR 1997 SC 1236 held that, it is in the domain of the Executive to acquire the land for specific NC: 2023:KHC-K:6253 purpose and the Court cannot direct the respondents to acquire the land and to award compensation.

entities.text: Ramanik Lal N Bhutta vs. State of Maharastra reported in AIR 1997 SC 1236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In view of the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforementioned decision, I am of the view that, the petitioner has not made out case for interference in this writ petition.
Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
